details: Found by the front 30 Oct: the VPS feature build-time-gates-on-the-vps-landing-gate-on-the is built in 4 changes (design rev 2, section 7); when change 2 landed, `relay land wt/build-time-gates-on-the-vps-landing-gate` printed 'closed build-time-gates-on-the-vps-landing-gate-on-the (feature, ip 90), landed on master at ea468ce7': lib/relay_land.py _close_features closes the feature item of any landed branch, so changes 3-5 lost their item and the front re-queued them by hand as a new item.
failing_case: A feature item taken by branch B; land B as an intermediate change: the item is closed on master.
pass_cases: an intermediate landing leaves the feature open and taken
the last landing closes it as today
reason: Landing a feature branch closes the item only without --keep-open; the original Q1 test is in the branch and passes.
findings.summary: relay land closes a feature after its first change

details: CONFIRMED by reproduction. _landed skips _close_features only for this call, but leaves the item in the exact state that
relay_lanes.lanes_state classifies as landed_open (taken, and landing() finds wt/x's fast-forward in the reflog). close_landed
closes every landed_open feature, and it runs (a) in the front's lanes hook right after the very landing Bash command with
--keep-open, in an ordinary front session, and (b) inside every later landing of any branch. So in the real flow the
feature is closed seconds after the intermediate landing, which is the failing case of the queue item. The new test passes
only because the test harness runs no hook and no second landing.
Also: the left state is a dead end for change 3: `relay queue start feat` refuses "taken by wt/x; release it first", and wt/x
no longer exists.
Size: 30 min.
evidence: Probe (scratchpad review-keepopen/test_keepopen_probe.py, ReviewFixes fixture): land wt/x --keep-open -> exit 0, then
plugins/front/hooks/lanes.py:103 LANDING regex matches "relay land " commands
lib/relay_queue.py:929 "queue item '{slug}' is taken by {taken_by}; release it first"
failing_case: Feature item feat taken by wt/x; land wt/x with --keep-open: it lands and leaves feat taken (the new test stops here).
Then relay_lanes.close_landed(main) runs, which is exactly what the front's PostToolUse lanes hook does after any Bash
command matching the landing regex (plugins/front/hooks/lanes.py:157, LANDING at line 103), and what _close_features does
on the landing of any other branch. Now: feat is closed (state "done") with wt/x's sha. Should: feat stays not closed.
fix_hint: Record the intermediate landing on the item itself, so every reader sees it, instead of skipping one sweep. Smallest: on
--keep-open, after the fast-forward, write a dated event to the feature item (the landed sha and branch) and release the
take, or keep the take but make relay_lanes.landing/lanes_state not count a landing that the item records as kept open.
Either way close_landed then leaves it alone, and the next change can take it. Keep the per-branch scope: --keep-open
should hold only this branch's item; other landed features still close in the sweep.
pass_cases: 1. feat (feature) taken by wt/x; land wt/x with --keep-open, then relay_lanes.close_landed(main): feat state is not "done".
2. Same, then a second branch wt/y with no item lands without the flag: feat is still not closed; the land output names no "closed feat".
3. Same, then lanes_state(main).landed_open does not list feat (the lanes line does not say "landed, still open: feat").
4. feat taken by wt/x; land wt/x with no flag: feat is closed with the landed sha, as today.
5. fix item taken by wt/x; land wt/x with --keep-open: the fix item's state is unchanged (still taken, closed only by the cycle's --test).
findings.summary: --keep-open only skips this one sweep: the front's lanes hook and the next landing close the kept-open feature anyway

details: CONFIRMED by reading. The queue item asks that "the cycle unit or relay land says whether this landing finishes the item";
only the CLI got the flag. In relay mode the cycle's land stage is the default lander (DEFAULTS land: true), so the change
does not reach the path where the reported failure happened unless the front knows to stop the cycle at ready. Principle 10
(works for a newcomer): an option a fresh session cannot find from relay's own texts. UNIT_KEYS has no field for it.
Size: 15 min.
evidence: plugins/delegate/workflows/cycle.js:288 the land command: branch and -C only
grep -rn keep-open over lib, bin, plugins, tests: only bin/relay, lib/relay_land.py and the one test.
failing_case: The front runs the cycle for change 2 of a 4-change feature with the default land: true. The land stage starts the landing
command of cycle.js:288 with no flag and no unit field to ask for one, so the feature is closed: the exact case of the queue
item. The front skill and delegate skill never mention --keep-open, so a fresh front does not know to set land: false and
land by hand with the flag.
fix_hint: Add a unit key (keep_open) to UNIT_KEYS and append --keep-open to the land command when it is set; one line in the front
skill's landing paragraph naming when to set it.
pass_cases: 1. A cycle unit for an intermediate change of a feature (for example a unit field keep_open: true) lands with --keep-open:
the command the land runner starts contains --keep-open.
2. A unit with no such field lands with the same command as today.
3. The front skill text (where it describes landing) has a line naming when to use --keep-open (an intermediate change of
a feature built in several changes).
reason: tests/test_cycle_workflow.py:754 passes; errors without the fix.
findings.summary: the cycle, which lands ready units by default, has no way to pass --keep-open, and no front text says when to use it

details: CONFIRMED by reading: `closed = [] if keep_open else _close_features(main)` drops the sweep for all items. Correct for the
common single-lane case, fragile otherwise. Likely solved together with F1 if the fix is per item. Size: 10 min.
failing_case: Feature other, taken by wt/z, was merged earlier and is still open (its close failed); landing wt/x with --keep-open closes
nothing at all, so other stays open too. Also landing wt/y with --keep-open, where wt/y holds a fix item or no item, gives
no word that the flag did nothing.
fix_hint: Keep the sweep and exclude only the landed branch's own feature item; say in the output which item was kept open.
pass_cases: 1. other (feature, wt/z landed earlier, still open) and feat (wt/x); land wt/x with --keep-open: other is closed, feat is not.
2. wt/y with no item; land wt/y with --keep-open: lands, and the output says no feature item was kept open (or the flag is refused before the gate).
reason: tests/test_land.py:605 and :613 pass; both fail on c35a09de^.
findings.summary: --keep-open skips the whole close sweep, so other landed features stay open and a flag on a fix or itemless branch passes silently

details: Question for the owner. How it works: a queue item is "taken" by one branch; the landing deletes that branch. The owner's
pass case says the feature stays "open and taken". Taken by a branch that no longer exists is what the lanes code reads as
"landed, still open" (see F1), and it blocks the next change's start. Live example: the VPS feature, changes 3-5 had to be
re-queued by hand. Answer (a) makes the next change start with one command and avoids F1 by construction; (b) keeps the
owner's wording literally but needs a marker every reader honours and an extra release step per change.
Size: answer only; the fix sits in F1.
failing_case: After landing wt/x with --keep-open, feat is "taken by wt/x" but wt/x and its worktree are deleted by the landing. Change 3
runs `relay queue start feat`, which refuses: "taken by wt/x; release it first". The queue item's pass case says "open and taken".
fix_hint: Recommend (a): release the take and record the intermediate landing as a dated fact on the item.
pass_cases: 1. (a) released: after the intermediate landing feat is open, not taken, with a dated record of the landed sha; `relay queue start feat` starts change 3 at once.
2. (b) taken: feat stays taken by wt/x with a record of the intermediate landing; change 3 needs `relay queue release feat` then start, or start learns to accept it.
reason: A question for the owner: the fixer chose option (a) released, as the review recommended. The owner decides.
findings.summary: after an intermediate landing, should the feature stay taken by the deleted branch, or go back to open for the next change?
